data.source_title: Massive Transfusion Protocols: The Role of Aggressive Resuscitation Versus Product Ratio in Mortality Reduction
data.locator: Methods, cohort periods and time-to-product definition; Table 3; Results
data.source_setting: Stanford University Medical Center, county-designated ACS-verified Level I trauma center; trauma patients admitted through ED and receiving at least 10 PRBC units in first 24 h
data.source_n: 40 eligible pre-MTP and 37 eligible post-MTP patients; 4,223 and 4,414 trauma activations respectively
data.quantity: Mean minutes from patient presentation to first documented patient-specific crossmatched product transfused
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed retrospective cohort comparison associated MTP introduction with shorter mean time to first documented crossmatched product: RBC 115 to 71 min, plasma 254 to 169 min, platelets 418 to 241 min. Four uncrossmatched RBC units were already available at major trauma activations before and after; the defined endpoint concerns subsequent patient-specific crossmatched products. MTP also specified communication and system flow improvements.
data.limitations: Small, highly selected massive-transfusion trauma cohorts and nonrandomized protocol-era comparison. These are means from arrival to transfused product, not blood-bank preparation or release service times and not times for all ED patients.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent emergency release and subsequent patient-specific compatibility workflows as separate paths; MTP activation coordinates blood bank, trauma, and clinical teams and repeated product cycles. Do not use these cohort means as generic per-unit processing times.

data.source_title: Massive Transfusion Protocols: The Role of Aggressive Resuscitation Versus Product Ratio in Mortality Reduction
data.locator: Methods, protocol description and first-product endpoint; Table 3
data.source_setting: Stanford Level I trauma center, ED-activated massive-transfusion workflow
data.source_period: Protocol implemented July 2005; evaluated across two-year pre and post cohorts
data.source_n: 77 selected patients meeting >=10 PRBC units in first 24 hours (40 pre; 37 post)
data.quantity: Blood-product availability workflow domains and observed first crossmatched product timing
data.unit: workflow domains; minutes from presentation to documented crossmatched RBC transfusion
data.source_evidence_basis: The original paper distinguishes emergency uncrossmatched RBC availability from later patient-specific crossmatched products and defines its endpoint as first crossmatched product delivered, transfused, and documented. Workflow record only; numerical comparisons are captured in the companion product-delay record.
data.limitations: The endpoint combines multiple steps and is not a blood-bank turnaround measure. Results apply to selected massive-transfusion trauma cases; process details and timing are center-specific.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Maintain separate states for emergency release versus completed type-and-screen/crossmatch; capture request, preparation, dispatch, receipt, transfusion, return/waste, and reconciliation timestamps if local data become available.
